source.title: Requiem, K. 626 — Dies irae
source.edition: Breitkopf & Härtel, 1877, edited by Johannes Brahms; Süssmayr completion
source.encoder: Martin Norbäck; 2014 update by Francisco Vila

bars.description: All 68 written bars once. Choir ends in bar65; the encoded orchestra continues through68, including the last lower string quarter-note at q269. No repeats or synthetic bass/continuo parts.

endpoints.basis: Independent pitch-energy inspection resolves the two final written quarters: the high D6/D5 tutti begins near 108.5 s, then the separate low D3/D4 string renewal follows near 109.0 s. The rejected broad-window candidate mistook the first chord for the last attack and compressed q268–269 to 0.081 s despite passing numeric gates. This narrow last search is a fitting constraint, not independent validation; no aural annotation.

anchors.basis: Final-bar upper D6 arrival follows the C-sharp6 leading tone near 108.3 s. This constrains the first final chord separately from the following low-string quarter; it is fitted pitch evidence, not an independent check.

provenance: Original Mutopia orchestral/SATB score and published MIDI retained byte-for-byte; this is the Brahms-edited 1877 Süssmayr completion, not an autograph-only attribution or a claim about Walter's marked performance parts.

Trumpets: trombe.ily writes C5/C4 and declares transposition d, producing published MIDI62/50 (range45–64). D trumpets sound a major second above the written pitch, so +12 restores74/62 and the proper sounding octave; engraving stays at written pitch. Independent transposition authority: https://utminers.utep.edu/charlesl/transpose.html ; separately reviewed by VerS.

F basset-horn transposition is already −7 and is retained. The clarinet-family section label explicitly names basset horns; they are not French horns. Other published MIDI pitches and chorus octaves remain unchanged.

The source has one Organo/orchestral-bass staff and no separately encoded cello, double-bass or trombone staves. Preserve its single written-pitch line rather than inventing doublings, octave layers or a continuo realisation. Source voice names identify notation, not separated instruments in the mono recording.
